answer: The protocol validates identities via a 1,024GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to reach the summit of the required memory state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting data through a complex umber color-shift filter; failure to return the ferrous signal of consistent memory responses triggers an immediate penalty. Honest agents pay 200 watts, while 1,000 fakes incur 200,000 watts, rendering pooling infeasible under current load.
